title: Is friction helpful or a nuisance?
examples: What are the disadvantages of friction?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Is this friction helpful or a nuisance?

explain.say: Imagine a world with no friction at all. You could not walk, because your shoes would slip. Your pencil would not write. Even a knot would slide undone. So friction can be a hero or a villain. Let us sort which is which.

draw.text: Is friction helpful or a nuisance?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Is this friction helpful or a nuisance?

explain.say: Look at the first group: helpful friction. Your shoes grip the ground so you can walk. Brakes rub the wheel to stop a bike. A pencil rubs off grey graphite onto paper. Can you think of one more helpful example from your day?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Is this friction helpful or a nuisance?

explain.say: Lovely, like gripping a cricket bat! Now the second group: nuisance friction. It wears down moving parts, like a bike chain, and turns useful energy into wasted heat. That is why machines get hot. Where would a squeaky door go?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Is this friction helpful or a nuisance?

explain.say: In the nuisance group, yes! To cut unwanted friction we use oil and grease, called lubricants, plus smooth surfaces and ball bearings. To boost helpful friction we add tyre treads, grip tape and rough soles.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Is this friction helpful or a nuisance?

explain.say: Super sorting! Wow fact: in curling, players sweep the ice in front of the stone. The rubbing warms the ice a tiny bit, cutting friction so the stone glides further. Challenge: count how many times friction helps you before breakfast.

faq.a: Friction lets us walk, grip things, stop vehicles, write and light matches. Without it everything would slip.
Use lubricants like oil or grease, make surfaces smoother, use ball bearings or wheels, and shape things to cut air resistance.
A lubricant is a slippery substance, like oil or grease, that sits between surfaces so they slide over each other easily.
asks: What does oil do in an engine?

faq.a: Friction between moving parts turns some of the useful energy into heat, which warms the machine and wastes energy.

faq.q: What would happen with no friction?
faq.a: You could not walk or hold things, cars could not start or stop, and nails and knots would not hold.

facts: Lubricants such as oil reduce friction and wear between moving parts.
Friction turns kinetic energy into heat, which is why rubbing your hands warms them.

quiz.say: Which is an example of helpful friction?
quiz.show: Which is an example of helpful friction?
quiz.why: Brakes use friction on purpose to slow the wheel safely.

wrong.1: That friction wastes energy and makes noise; oil fixes it.
wrong.2: Wear damages machines, so it is unwanted.

quiz.say: Why do we oil a bike chain?
quiz.show: Why do we oil a bike chain?
quiz.why: Oil is a lubricant: it lets the chain parts slide easily, so less energy is wasted and less wear happens.

wrong.0: Oil makes surfaces slippery, so it lowers grip.
wrong.2: A few drops of oil add almost no mass, and that is not the purpose.
